findings.title: The here-document row says the body's lines are still read; the extractor joins every later fence line into the refusal
findings.recommendation: Make the extractor do what the row says, or make the row say what the extractor does. Recommended: in extractFenceLines, join the next line only while the result is an OPEN QUOTE (`'open' in result`), never on a refusal, so a refused line fails alone at its own line and every later line of the fence is extracted and checked; then the row's 'its lines are still read' holds, and the substitution rows stop hiding later lines' defects behind one failure. Correct the test comment in surface-snippets.test.ts to match, and add a case: a refused line followed by an orbit line yields one failure and one snippet.
findings.reproduction: A throwaway test over analyseSurface with the fence ```bash / cat > m <<'EOF' / orbit status --change <n> / EOF / orbit validate <n> / ``` returned snippets: [] and ONE failure at line 2 whose snippet is all four lines joined. The same happens for `git log $(x)` followed by `orbit validate <n>`: no snippet, one failure joining both lines. Cause: extractFenceLines' `while (!result.ok && i + 1 < lines.length)` joins on ANY not-ok result, a refusal included (present since rc05, made reachable by the walk's new `<<` refusal). The spec row the walk wrote says 'the body is never delimited, so its lines are still read', and the test comment 'its lines are still read'.

walk_entry.title: Redirection handling does not satisfy the declared operator closure

commentary: This pass verified the two walks of the blind pair over each entry's sweep scope, and ran the residual check from the commit that added the external return: every file changed since sits in an entry's edit record. Both regressions are the same shape the pair itself found: a walk's claim about a mechanism stated beside it rather than in it. The capture's any-rejected reduction is real and tested, but the requirement that owns the capture's table never says it. The here-document row describes an extractor that reads the body, and a probe showed the extractor reads nothing after a refused line. That second one exposed an older behaviour: since rc05, a refusal joins the rest of the fence into one failure. That never hides a defect from a green sweep, since the fence already fails, but it does mean one failure masks the next. The tokenizer's new redirect and quoted-substitution branches held under every case I constructed, including a fd digit before `<`, `>&-`, and `>(` after a plain `>`.
